sections.text: The worlds, with the whole realm of creation, come and go; but, O Arjuna, whoso comes to Me, for him there is no rebirth.
Those who understand the cosmic day and cosmic night know that one day of creation is a thousand cycles, and that the night is of equal length.
At the dawning of that day all objects in manifestation stream forth from the Unmanifest, and when evening falls they are dissolved into It again.

We had been discussing chapter 8, Akshara Brahma Yoga Yoga of Imperishable Brahman this world which I live in has things and beings. Things have their production date or date of creation and will also have a date of destruction. Beings have their birth dates and will also have their death dates.
Nothing in this world remains permanently. Everything is perishable, exists for a limited period in both time and space. But this ever changing reality which I experience as the world cannot exist unless there is an imperishable substratum.
And Bhagavan said in this chapter that Brahman is that imperishable reality. Brahman is the truth which makes all other relative truths possible. For example, I can say this room exists. Thats a statement of truth.
But it only exists because the another universal truth exists. That is the room space existed before this room was built. It is right now here as room space and will remain space when this room will be destroyed.
So based on that universal reality which I call space, the relative reality, what I call room space can exist. Bhagavan says the Brahman in a similar way exists. As Bhagawan Shankaracharya says, the principle that graces all bodies is their essential self.
Any being will not be aware of his own self unless that principle, imperishable immortal principle is residing in that body. With that consciousness I become aware of my conditioning which I call my body, mind and intellect. And then Im aware of myself.
So it is the self-knowing reality -- the very nature of Brahman -- which makes me aware of myself as that conditioned self. Right now Im not aware of my supreme self that is imperishable, deathless, and birthless. But Im aware of myself as this limited body, limited mind, limited intellect -- as Nil Bhatt -- because of that consciousness which is functioning through me.
So Bhagavan says that that consciousness is now making you aware of your own limitations and also making you aware of the existence of this world of perishable nature. As long as I am conditioned and identified with this body, mind, and intellect, I will have all the limitations of this body, mind, and intellect. And therefore the sorrows, therefore unhappiness.
And therefore I feel bound by these limitations. My goal is to liberate myself from my limitations, my unhappiness, my sorrows and attain a state of bliss where there never will be any sorrow, never will be any limitations and never will be any unhappiness. Bhagavan said, that can only happen when you identify with me, the imperishable, and not with the one who is conditioned by your body, mind, and intellect.
As long as I remain aware of the limitations of the room, I will only be seeing the space as room space. But if I want to see this space as immortal -- If I never want to get this space destroyed, Ill be always afraid of what happens if someone destroys this building. If earthquake happens or a meteor falls on my property, well, it will be destroyed.
Is the room space getting destroyed? But right now Im more identified with the conditioning than the space itself. And therefore that fear of destruction. If my identification was not with the conditioning, just the space.
This is my land and this is my space, and I want to own this thing forever. But heres the thing: nothing can destroy the space itself. The only thing that can be destroyed is whatever you have built on that land.
The space will never be destroyed. But as long as my identification is with that building on that land, Ill be afraid. When my identification goes beyond that, then I will not be afraid of the destruction of the building.
So Bhagavan said, one who identifies with me will come to attain me. Antakale cha mam eva kalevaram ya prayati sa mad bhavam yati na asti atra sansayah. There is no doubt that one who gives up this identification with body, mind, and intellect -- treating the leaving of this identification as the death -- and thinking about me alone, will come to me.
There is no doubt about that. So the advice we have seen so far says: therefore, tasmat sarveshu kaleshu mam anusmara yudhya cha -- engage in this battle of life constantly remembering me as your true self. Not this conditioned self as your true self, but me, the imperishable, who is making it possible for you to function.
Fight this battle of life with that in mind, and you shall be liberated from these limitations. You will come to be one with me, and once you become one with me, after that there is no coming and going again. Mam upetya punar janma dukhalayam ashashvatam na apnuvanti.
Having attained me, there is no coming and going back to this house of pain we call this world. But now Bhagavan says, in a stark contrast to the ones who have identified with me and one who has become one with me. If youre striving to achieve that liberation but havent reached that prerequisite qualification, then you will constantly come back and forth.
So the next verse 16 says, A Brahma Bhuvanat lokah punaravartino Arjuna Mam upetya tu Kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate -- all the worlds up to the world of Brahmaji, Brahmaloka, are subject to birth and rebirth. Punara vartina -- constantly coming again and again, coming back to the same cycle. One who reaches me, there is no rebirth for him.
So what does that mean, reaching up to the world of Brahmaji? Brahmaji is the creator. As we know in our Hindu Trinity, Brahma is the creator, Vishnu is the sustainer and Shiva is the destroyer. This creation, sustenance, and destruction is constantly going on in this world.
Brahma is the ultimate creator of this entire universe. In our concept of Hiranyagarbha in Vedanta, Brahma represents the ultimate creator -- the total mind and total intellect. I am the creator of my own world.
You are the creator of your world, and she is the creator of her world. We create our world through our mind and intellect, depending on our desires and vasanas. Now, if I take this group and look at it as one -- individually we have our vasanas and desires, but we also have group vasanas and desires.
So well say, well, when are we going to have the Janmastami next? So everybody will say, well, I would like to have it on such and such and lets do this and lets do that. These common thoughts put together what we call it a planning, a group planning will have group activity. So thats a mind which is expanded from my mind to a groups mind.
You can continue to expand this mind and intellect, including more and more people and beings into it. When you reach the ultimate limit of all the beings and things, all the minds and intellects put together -- that is Brahmaji, Brahma the creator. When my identification rises from me to my family, to my neighborhood, to my community, Im expanding my identity and including them as my own self.
So I may be making progress in my spiritual evolution by expanding my identity, but until I reach that pre-qualifying limit, I still have to come back over and over again. Well, it is something like this. If you are taking any licensing examination -- for those of you who are professionals who have to take the licensing exam, you probably know all about it.
I took mine in this country when I came here in 1984, and I knew that it was going to be difficult because I had barely come here, had no experience in this country, and people had already warned me: its going to take you a long time to get this license, simply because there were nine parts to the exam and you have to clear all nine parts to get a license. So the firm I had joined initially a large firm, and there were at least about a couple of hundred people, at least at any given year, there are about 60 to 80 people taking exams. So they told me, Take it easy, Rajan.
You just came to this country; its going to take you eight to ten years before you can pass this exam. And I said, What do you mean by that? I dont understand what youre saying. Why should it take so long? They said, Well, here is how it works. Youll take the exams and probably pass maybe two parts out of nine. Then you will come back next year and may pass another couple of parts, then come back the year after and may pass one or two. People who experienced this had formulated an average: it takes about six to ten years for somebody to get licensed as an architect in this country after graduating from architecture school.
Because until you pass all nine parts -- and if you fail any one subject more than three times, you take all nine parts all over again. There were some people I knew who had already given up taking these licensing exams. I said, Well, all you have to do is pass all nine parts and it will be fine. They said, Yeah, that sounds easy, but it is not. That was obviously their perception.
So they go, take the exam, come back, take the exam and come back -- till you reach a point when the ninth part is cleared, then you get a license. And even after passing all nine parts and getting a license, you still have to maintain your continuing education to remain effective as an architect. This is something like our spiritual journey.
Bhagavan said that we are all pursuing our spiritual evolution as seekers, reaching from the level we are at right now to the next level as we make more progress. But at the time of death, if my evolution has not risen to the level where I can be liberated, Ill have to come back -- just as with the exams. If I havent cleared all nine parts, I have to come back next year to clear whatever parts are left.
Same way, in our spiritual journey, things we have learned and things yet to be learned will decide how many times I have to come back. This is driven by my desires and vasanas. My desires will make me come back to that state, that stage where I feel comfortable that I can make progress from here.
After I pass my high school graduation, I go to undergraduate school. I cannot just say, After my high school graduation, leave me alone -- my education is finished. To get to a doctorate level, I have to make my own efforts. So up to the world of Brahmaji.
In the world of Brahmaji, you have the identification with this entire creation. And in the concept of gradual liberation, Karma Mukti, which is accepted in Vedanta, it basically says that karma with Upasana can lead you to the realm of Brahmaji. If you do your karma diligently with devotion to the Lord, you will reach a state of identification where you will feel the whole world is your own being and you reach the world of Brahmaji.
Once reaching that, there is no coming back. From that, you will just merge into the supreme Brahman.

A Brahma bhuvana lokah punar avartino Arjuna, even up to the world of Brahma, all realms are subject to return. This teaching shatters any notion of a permanent heavenly destination short of complete liberation. The analogy of professional licensing examinations is illuminating: just as you must pass all nine parts to become a licensed architect, you must complete your entire spiritual curriculum to achieve liberation. Failing any part means returning to retake it. Consider your own spiritual exam results: What subjects have you mastered? What areas still need work? Patience, forgiveness, non-attachment, selfless service, which of these do you still struggle with? Each challenge in life is an examination. Each failure is simply an invitation to return and try again until mastery is achieved.
The cosmic scale presented here, one day of Brahma equals a thousand yugas, approximately 4.32 billion years, puts our earthly concerns in perspective. Your current frustrations, achievements, and dramas are occurring within a cosmic blink. Verse 18 describes how all beings stream forth at the dawn of Brahmas day and dissolve back into the unmanifest at cosmic night. Your individual existence is part of this vast breathing rhythm of the universe. This week, practice holding this expanded perspective when you encounter stress or conflict. Ask yourself: In the scale of Brahmas day, how significant is this problem? This is not to dismiss your real concerns, but to loosen the grip of identification. The teaching points to the one place beyond this cosmic rhythm: Mam upetya tu Kaunteya punar janma na vidyate, reaching Me, there is no rebirth. What would it mean to identify with the eternal witness of this cosmic dance rather than being swept along as a participant?
